title: Adaptive Kernel Negotiator with Sparse-Attention Aware Bucketing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce wasted compute from padding across mixed-length workloads by combining sequence-length clustering with an online kernel selector that negotiates per-batch kernel choices based on latency/cost/quality signals. This ticket covers design, a lightweight runtime prototype, and an A/B benchmark against the current length-bucketing stack.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end prototype that performs online bucketing and selects kernels per output micro-batch. 2) Measured token-cost reduction >= 12% on production-like request traces at 95th-percentile load without regression in p99 latency > 10%. 3) Observability: per-route breakdown of chosen kernel, bucket size distribution, and pad-elimination rate. 4) Safe rollout path with canary and automatic fallback to baseline kernel on error/latency regression.
implementation_notes:
- Components:
  * Online bucketer: stream-oriented sliding-window clusterer that assigns incoming requests to active buckets based on effective decoding horizon. Buckets have dynamic thresholds tuned by recent load and model memory pressure.
  * Kernel negotiator: a scoring function that weighs kernel throughput model, expected KV-cache footprint, and anticipated tail-latency risk. It emits a kernel_hint tag for the runtime (e.g., FLASH_ATTENTION_V2, TRITON_MATMUL, INT8_FUSED).
  * Prefill-aware scheduler: when prefill-heavy traffic detected, prioritize larger coalescing windows but bias towards kernels with high prefill throughput. During decode-heavy spikes, tighten coalescing to favor low-latency kernels.
- Data needed: per-kernel throughput and memory models precomputed by benchmarking harness (seqlen x batchsize x model_variant).
- Fallback rules: if negotiation fails or kernel reports errors, tag batch with FALLBACK_BASELINE and record metric.
- Safety: ensure negotiation never increases tensor memory beyond node capacity; include quick-reject if predicted memory > 95% node limit.
benchmarks:
Planned benchmarks:
- Trace A (interactive agent traffic): measure token-cost and p99 latency for baseline vs negotiator across 1M requests.
- Trace B (mixed long-form generation): evaluate pad reduction and KV-cache hit amplification.
- Ablations: negotiator without sparse-attention awareness, and bucketer with static thresholds.
Target metrics: token-cost delta, p95/p99 latency delta, pad-elimination rate, kernel-switch frequency.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge prototype behind feature flag (runtime flag: kernel_negotiator_v1).
2) Canary on 2% traffic targeting non-critical routes for 48h. Monitor p95/p99, error-rate, kernel-switch churn.
3) Expand to 20% if stable, compare economics for 7 days.
4) Full rollout after cost-benefit sign-off and PM approval with migration notes.
Rollback: feature-flag toggle and automatic disable if p99 latency or error-rate exceed thresholds for >10 minutes.
